newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana to sell "solidarity" bananas in Holland.
newsitem.headline: Ghana to sell "solidarity" bananas in Holland.

text.p: Ghana's sole banana exporter, in a bid to stave off bankruptcy, has co-founded a Dutch company to sell its bananas as "solidarity" bananas in the Netherlands, according to its managing director.

Hans van den Broek told Reuters the annual 4,000-5,000 tonnes production of Volta River Estates Ltd (VREL) would be marketed by the new company Agrofer BV under the auspices -- and hallmark -- of Dutch fair trade organisation Max Havelaar.
"If this fails, we are finished, kaputt," he said on Thursday, adding he lacked funds to pay the 830 workers.
Dutch interests and a handful of Ghanaians own VREL. A banana-ripening company, Dutch fair trade organisation Solidaridad and VREL, each own a third of Agrofer BV, which was founded on Wednesday.
VREL has 600 acres of banana plantations at Akosombo on the shores of the Volta River (92 km northeast of Accra).

Fair trade organisations in Europe and the United States market produce from farmers' cooperatives and companies in developing countries which promote environmentally sustainable production and fair wages and working conditions.
Max Havelaar's director Hans Bolscher said during a recent visit that VREL paid its workers relatively well and made minimal use of pesticides and fungicides.
Van den Broek, a Dutch national, took over VREL's management in 1993. Thus far, the company's main market has been France.
Van den Broek said the first Ghanaian "solidarity" bananas will be presented to Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok in Rotterdam on November 18.
